title: Bodhavilāsa — Play of Knowledge
author: Kṣemarāja
text:
The Bodhavilāsa is a hymn of five songs by Kṣemarāja (c. tenth–eleventh century), opening with a double invocation — to Netra and to Śiva in his fivefold act — before unfolding its doctrine. It concerns the free cause, so called although it is in no way deficient or optional, and the powers that proceed from it: creation, preservation, dissolution, and the concealment and release by which the world is veiled and revealed.

Its juice: the cause is called free precisely because nothing compels its play. Kṣemarāja's point is that bondage is not the world's making but its misreading — the powers are the Lord's own movement, and knowledge (bodha) is the name for catching that movement mid-play rather than judging it from outside.
